A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAN: Fourier Analysis Networks and contain 21 readable pages. The text, equations, Figures 1–10, Tables 1–11, and Appendices A–F support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original function-fitting, forecasting, sentiment-classification, and image-recognition experiments, plus additional empirical results including Burgers’ equation experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices. Their retention from v4 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The FAN layer in Equation 9, stacked architecture in Equations 10–11, gated variant, and substitutions into Transformer and CNN architectures are unchanged. No algorithmic component or procedure is revised.

E1.justification: The evaluated tasks and datasets remain unchanged, including image recognition in Table 4 and the appendix forecasting and Burgers’ equation experiments. The newly mentioned gravitational-wave, EEG, and large-language-model applications are attributed to other papers, not evaluated here.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. This includes the general neural-network baselines, FNN/FSNN/FTNN in Table 5, FNO in Table 8, direct coefficient learning in Table 9, FEDformer in Table 10, and Snake in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training settings. For example, forecasting still uses 96 input steps and prediction horizons of 96, 192, 336, and 720 steps.

E4.justification: The coefficient-learning comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity, depth analysis, instance-normalization analysis, and OOD tests are retained. Appendices B.3–B.5, B.7, and D provide the same analytical questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed or repeated-run counts or formal significance tests. The existing statistical reporting and plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results match, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains Transformer/FAN average MSE values of 0.994/0.839, and Table 3 retains their SST-2 accuracies of 81.19/81.54.

T1.justification: The Fourier-series derivation, formal network definitions in Equations 1–14, complexity expressions in Table 1, and universal-approximation argument in Appendix E are unchanged.

C1.justification: v5’s abstract explicitly claims that FAN overcomes depth-scaling difficulties to enable large-scale models, strengthening v4’s framing around architectural scalability and potential use in foundational models. The central periodicity, general-purpose modeling, and efficiency contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the same interpretations concerning expressive power, extrapolation, hidden periodicity, and learning efficiency. Replacing its unresolved figure reference with Dong et al. (2025) changes the attribution without changing the argument. No substantive limitation or mechanism explanation is added.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same hardware, optimizers, hyperparameters, data-generation instructions, and architecture details. The code-access footnote is unchanged; no new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Sections 6–7 newly cite FANformer, gravitational-wave analysis, and EEG emotion recognition to position FAN’s subsequent applications. The bibliography also adds Dong et al. (2024) and Wan et al. (2013), while removing Bassey et al. (2021) and Mildenhall et al. (2020). Section 5’s substantive account of earlier approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 partially rewrites the abstract and conclusion, renames Section 7 'Conclusion and Future Work,' replaces the broken 'Figure ??' reference, and reorders/reformats the bibliography. The main technical narrative and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts table placement and paragraph breaks, particularly on pages 8–10, and changes the bibliography layout. Figures 1–10 retain identical graphics, and all table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: Replacing Section 6’s unresolved 'Figure ??' with an identifiable citation and adding attributed follow-up applications modestly improve traceability and research context. The method, experimental evidence, theory, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The stronger scalability wording is not accompanied by new in-paper scaling experiments, so the quality gain is limited.
